sources.entry: hypercorn - An ASGI and WSGI server based on Hyper libraries and inspired by Gunicorn.

summary.one_liner: Hypercorn is an ASGI and WSGI web server built on the sans-io hyper, h11, h2, and wsproto libraries, inspired by Gunicorn.
summary.what_it_does: Serves ASGI and WSGI applications over HTTP/1, HTTP/2, and WebSockets (over HTTP/1 and HTTP/2). It can run on asyncio, uvloop, or trio worker types. Optional HTTP/3 support uses the aioquic library and is enabled by installing the h3 extra and choosing a QUIC binding such as --quic-bind. It can be run from the command line with "hypercorn module:app" or embedded in Python code via hypercorn.asyncio.serve or a Trio example. Hypercorn originated as part of the Quart framework and was split out into a standalone server, forked from Quart 0.5.0.
use_cases: embed an async web server in a Python program
deploy Quart or other ASGI frameworks
notable: Supports both ASGI and WSGI applications from one server
Choice of asyncio, uvloop, or trio worker types
Built on sans-io protocol libraries (hyper, h11, h2, wsproto)
Originated as part of Quart and was forked from its 0.5.0 release
caveats: HTTP/3 support requires installing an optional extra and choosing a QUIC binding
